summary: GOLDEN LABEL, hand-drafted against the PDF. FATF study of how proceeds from illegal logging, illegal mining and waste trafficking are laundered: co-mingling of illegal with legal goods early in the supply chain, front companies in cash-intensive export sectors (vanilla, hair salons, waste management), shell companies and nominees hiding beneficial owners behind offshore and layered structures, trade-based fraud (falsified shipping documents, mislabelled waste and timber, under-declared exports, false invoices simulating trade), third-party wire transfers under the guise of payments for goods, hawala and underground exchange dealers, cash couriers, and PEP-linked corruption around concessions. Worked cases from South Africa, Madagascar, Italy, Brazil, Chile/US (NTR Metals), China, DRC (Gertler) and Guinea (Steinmetz), with an Annex A of risk indicators.

In some cases, criminals relied on front companies in other cash intensive sectors not linked to natural resources.

This includes integrating proceeds through third party wire transfers under the guise of payments for goods and services, but also investments and sponsorship.
These hairdressers imported hair through a TBML scheme run by the illegal miners and a professional criminal group, with the criminals invoicing the hairdressers for importing on their behalf.

extraction_notes: Golden label. The predicates (illegal logging, mining, waste trafficking) are not typologies; only the laundering methods are labelled. Front companies are labelled BA007, not SAN004: the report is not sanctions-framed and its front companies are real cash-intensive businesses used as cover, so the sanctions twin convention does not apply; the physical co-mingling of goods is emergent. TBML004 at medium: the Italian USD 68m false invoices simulate trade that never happened, which is phantom shipping rather than a governed 'false invoicing' entry. TBML001 not labelled: 'over or under declare' and 'higher declared values' on p58 are one indicator each. SAN008 kept for the repeated offshore-arbitrage theme despite the family. Considered and dropped as single mentions: correspondent-banking nesting (p25), sports sponsorship (p33), PAT009 transfer pricing, PAT001, BA005, BA006 (Annex A). Mr. L, Ms. C, Country A/B kingpin and the Madagascar networks are anonymised and not actors; enforcement bodies (FBI, Guardia di Finanza, SAMIFIN, FIUs) are not actors. CH, NL, SG, DE, NO appear as prosecuting, regulating or donor states and are not jurisdictions; GN is where Steinmetz's bribes sat. REVIEWED 2026-09-11. Added TBML001 Over Invoicing at LOW. p31 names both directions in one sentence -- 'the trend to over or under declare goods being shipped' -- which is the sentence this label already cited for TBML002U, so the twin was evidenced and unlabelled, the same asymmetry corrected in ADV-2026-0003. LOW rather than medium because the asymmetry is real: under-invoicing also has p58's specific 'exported at below market prices', where over-declaration has only the shared generic phrase. That matches the report's emphasis -- environmental crime undervalues exports. Omissions otherwise: TBML003, BA001, BA003, BA004, PAT001 and PAT005 are absent. The predicate crimes (illegal logging, mining, waste trafficking) are correctly NOT labelled as typologies; the library holds laundering methods, not predicates. BA007 Cash Intensive Activity is CORRECT here -- p29/p30 name cash intensive sectors explicitly.
